days.title: Nationalisation
days.desc: Key industries and utilities owned by the state.
days.note: Putting industry in public hands is a left-wing idea. It says little about personal freedom, so it sits at the centre line.
days.source: Manifesto Project Dataset 2026a (Lehmann et al.), derived · 360 manifestos in 58 countries

days.title: Deregulating markets
days.desc: Removing government rules on how businesses operate.
days.note: Cutting red tape is a favourite of the economic right. It says little about personal freedom, so it stays close to the middle vertically.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 24 parties in 18 countries

days.title: Self-reliance over welfare
days.desc: People look after themselves, with less redistribution by the state.
days.note: Expecting people to look after themselves is the mirror image of redistribution. It sits well to the right, with a mild authoritarian tilt.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 13 parties in 10 countries

days.title: Secular government
days.desc: Religion kept out of law and public policy.
days.note: Keeping religion out of lawmaking is backed by liberal parties, mostly centre-left.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 87 parties in 27 countries

days.title: Fighting corruption
days.desc: Making the clean-up of politics a top priority.
days.note: Almost every party says it wants a cleaner politics, so this lands close to the middle.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 32 parties in 13 countries

days.title: Women's rights policies
days.desc: Equal pay, parental leave and similar policies.
days.note: Equal pay and parental leave are championed mostly by left-leaning, socially liberal parties.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 68 parties in 24 countries

days.title: Wealth redistribution
days.desc: Taxing and transferring from richer to poorer people to narrow inequality.
days.note: Taking from the wealthy to help everyone else is the classic left-wing idea. The parties behind it also tend to be socially liberal, so it sits low as well as far left.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 33 parties in 20 countries

days.title: Environment over growth
days.desc: Protecting nature even at some cost to economic growth.
days.note: Protecting nature even at some economic cost is a left and liberal position, and Green parties lead on it.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 37 parties in 21 countries

days.title: Assimilation
days.desc: Newcomers are expected to adopt the majority culture.
days.note: Expecting newcomers to adopt the local culture is backed mostly by authoritarian parties, with a mild lean to the right.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 69 parties in 30 countries

days.title: Rural interests
days.desc: Policy that puts the countryside ahead of cities.
days.note: Putting the countryside first is mostly a traditional, authoritarian position, with a small lean right.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 23 parties in 14 countries

days.title: Trade unions
days.desc: Support for organised labour and workers' collective rights.
days.note: Backing for organised labour is a left-wing idea that sits about level on personal freedom.
days.source: Manifesto Project Dataset 2026a (Lehmann et al.), derived · 360 manifestos in 55 countries

days.title: Urban interests
days.desc: Policy that puts cities ahead of the countryside.
days.note: Putting cities first is a liberal position, with a mild lean to the right.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 15 parties in 8 countries

days.title: Strong executive
days.desc: Leaders can act without heavy constraint.
days.note: Letting leaders act without heavy constraint is authoritarian at heart, and it appeals to parties across the economic spectrum.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 34 parties in 16 countries

days.title: Human rights and freedoms
days.desc: Personal freedom, civil rights and the rule of law.
days.note: Parties that talk most about human rights are liberal, with almost no economic lean.
days.source: Manifesto Project Dataset 2026a (Lehmann et al.), derived · 360 manifestos in 49 countries

days.title: Liberal immigration
days.desc: Easy rules for people to move to and settle in a country.
days.note: Open-door parties lean left and are strongly liberal on personal freedom. It's one of the clearest low-and-left ideas.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 17 parties in 12 countries

days.title: Free movement across borders
days.desc: Goods, services, capital and workers move freely between member countries.
days.note: Letting goods, services and workers move freely appeals to the centre and centre-right, with a lean liberal.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 90 parties in 26 countries

days.title: Same-sex marriage
days.desc: Legal marriage for couples of the same sex.
days.note: Like wider LGBTQ+ rights, this is a socially liberal idea with only a mild economic lean.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 100 parties in 27 countries

days.title: Independent judiciary
days.desc: Courts that governments cannot direct.
days.note: Almost every party says it backs independent courts, so this sits near the middle, leaning a little liberal.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 130 parties in 27 countries

days.title: Leaving international unions
days.desc: Countries take back powers from shared bodies.
days.note: Taking powers back from shared bodies is backed by nationalist, authoritarian parties, mostly a bit right of centre.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 35 parties in 20 countries

days.title: Limits on leaders
days.desc: Checks and balances that constrain those in power.
days.note: Checks and balances are favoured by liberal parties, more often on the left.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 19 parties in 12 countries

days.title: Nationalism
days.desc: National identity and sovereignty come first.
days.note: Putting the nation first is the signature of authoritarian parties, most of whom lean right on economics.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 60 parties in 28 countries

days.title: LGBTQ+ rights
days.desc: Legal protection and equal treatment for LGBTQ+ people.
days.note: Backed by socially liberal parties, mostly on the centre-left, so it sits low and a little left.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 80 parties in 27 countries

days.title: Equality
days.desc: Fairer outcomes and treatment for all groups in society.
days.note: Parties that talk about fairness and equal treatment lean left and liberal.
days.source: Manifesto Project Dataset 2026a (Lehmann et al.), derived · 360 manifestos in 50 countries

days.title: Public services first
days.desc: Spending more on public services in preference to cutting taxes.
days.note: Parties that put hospitals and schools ahead of tax cuts sit well to the left, and most are socially liberal too.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 42 parties in 22 countries

days.title: Civil liberties first
days.desc: Strong limits on state power, even if it makes fighting crime harder.
days.note: Putting freedoms ahead of security is a libertarian instinct. It leans left because left-wing parties are the ones leading on it today.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 40 parties in 20 countries

days.title: Strict immigration limits
days.desc: Tight caps and controls on how many people may enter.
days.note: The parties pushing hardest for limits are strongly authoritarian, but they come from both sides on the economy. So it sits high up and only slightly right.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 70 parties in 30 countries

days.title: Military strength
days.desc: Spending on and support for the armed forces.
days.note: Parties that give the armed forces a lot of attention lean right and a little authoritarian.
days.source: Manifesto Project Dataset 2026a (Lehmann et al.), derived · 360 manifestos in 54 countries

days.title: Deeper international union
days.desc: Countries pool more sovereignty in a shared body.
days.note: Pooling more power in a shared body is backed by centrist, liberal-leaning parties.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 114 parties in 31 countries

days.title: Trade protectionism
days.desc: Tariffs and rules that shield domestic producers.
days.note: This one splits the middle. Left parties protect jobs and nationalist right parties protect industry, so it lands near the centre line but high on the grid.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 35 parties in 16 countries

days.title: Regulated markets
days.desc: Strong government rules on how businesses operate.
days.note: Strong rules on business are a left-wing instinct, and the parties behind them are mostly socially liberal.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 28 parties in 17 countries

days.title: Anti-militarism
days.desc: Cutting military spending and favouring disarmament and peace.
days.note: Parties that stress peace and disarmament lean left and a little liberal.
days.source: Manifesto Project Dataset 2026a (Lehmann et al.), derived · 360 manifestos in 50 countries

days.title: Traditional morality
days.desc: Law and public life that uphold traditional moral values.
days.note: Parties that talk most about traditional values are strongly authoritarian and lean right.
days.source: Manifesto Project Dataset 2026a (Lehmann et al.), derived · 360 manifestos in 56 countries

days.title: Multiculturalism
days.desc: Different cultures keep their own identities within one society.
days.note: Parties that welcome many cultures living side by side lean left and liberal.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 24 parties in 17 countries

days.title: Anti-establishment politics
days.desc: Attacking elites and the political establishment.
days.note: Attacking elites is a populist theme. It sits high on the grid and close to the middle on the economy because both left and right do it.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 49 parties in 26 countries

days.title: Free trade
days.desc: Few barriers to buying and selling across borders.
days.note: Open borders for goods and services means fewer state controls, which makes it right-leaning and liberal.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 15 parties in 11 countries

days.title: Tough on crime
days.desc: Stronger policing and harsher sentences, even at some cost to civil liberties.
days.note: Harsher policing and sentences are pushed by authoritarian parties from across the economic spectrum, so it sits high and only a bit right.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 55 parties in 27 countries

days.title: Expanding education
days.desc: More public spending on schools and universities.
days.note: Spending more on schools and universities is mildly left, and it's backed from across the spectrum.
days.source: Manifesto Project Dataset 2026a (Lehmann et al.), derived · 360 manifestos in 53 countries

days.title: Religion in politics
days.desc: Religious principles shape law and public policy.
days.note: Parties that want faith to shape the law are strongly traditional, so it sits near the top. It has little to say about economics.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 34 parties in 17 countries

days.title: International authority over security
days.desc: A union of countries sets shared foreign and defence policy.
days.note: Parties that want a shared foreign and defence policy lean slightly liberal, and they come from all along the economic line.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 24 parties in 15 countries

days.title: Government sway over judges
days.desc: Elected governments get a say in judicial decisions and appointments.
days.note: Wanting politicians to have a say over courts is a strongly authoritarian stance, with a mild lean right.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 12 parties in 8 countries

days.title: Centralised government
days.desc: Decisions made nationally, with less power for regions.
days.note: Parties that want decisions made nationally are strongly authoritarian, with little economic lean.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 16 parties in 11 countries

days.title: Growth over environment
days.desc: Economic growth takes priority over environmental protection.
days.note: Putting the economy first is right-leaning. In practice the parties that do it are also traditional and authoritarian.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 25 parties in 17 countries

days.title: Direct democracy
days.desc: Citizens decide big issues by referendum rather than leaving them to representatives.
days.note: Letting the public decide big questions by referendum is mostly a populist idea. Populists sit high on the grid but all over the economic spectrum.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 26 parties in 14 countries

days.title: Cosmopolitanism
days.desc: People are citizens of the world first, and borders matter less.
days.note: Seeing yourself as a citizen of the world is a liberal, left-leaning outlook.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 40 parties in 22 countries

days.title: Cutting taxes
days.desc: Lowering taxes even if public services receive less money.
days.note: Tax cuts are backed by the economic right, often alongside parties that favour traditional values. That pulls it a little way up the grid.
days.source: CHES 2024 issue scores, derived (Rovny et al. 2025) · 27 parties in 16 countries
